summary: Pins the two copies of the kb write spec shapes together: the canonical WRITE_GUIDE_SHAPES and the copy hooks/capture-payload.mjs inlines into the capture prompt. It exists because they already drifted — the inlined flow shape lost "aliases" and the notes written from it were reachable only by their exact title. REQUIRED is a FINDABILITY list, not the schema: the fields a note cannot be retrieved without (file-single needs path/summary/aliases/symbols, flow needs title/aliases/summary/steps). It imports the .mjs hook directly and calls buildCapturePayload with a stub worklist, so it tests the real rendered prompt rather than a fixture — meaning it also writes that stub session's manifest to tmpdir as a side effect. Add a field to one copy and this test fails until the other has it too.

summary: Pins every consumer to hooks/note-shape.mjs so a required field cannot go missing from one surface again. Rewritten 2026-08-01 from 'two copies agree' to 'every surface renders from the table': it asserts each spec example contains the fields its own checksForSpec demands, that the write guide and capture prompt both contain each example's first line VERBATIM (proving the text came from the table rather than a copy typed alongside it), that the MCP kb_write description contains requiredFieldsLine() and the word aliases, and that kb_repair is in TOOL_DEFINITIONS. One suite exists purely to stop a regression from returning: no surface may say a flow's anchors come from its steps — it greps the guide, the capture prompt and flowStepsWarning's own output for that phrase. Note the tools array is exported as TOOL_DEFINITIONS, not KB_TOOLS.

summary: Pins every consumer to hooks/note-shape.mjs so a required field cannot go missing from one surface again: each spec example must contain the fields its own checksForSpec demands, the write guide and capture prompt must both carry every example verbatim, the MCP kb_write description must contain requiredFieldsLine(), and a dedicated suite asserts no surface says a flow's anchors come from its steps. It also carries the write-time warning contracts, and those are the ones to extend when a new WARN is added: two sibling suites, 'flowStepsWarning judges the folded note, not the spec' and 'missingFieldsWarning judges the folded note, not the spec', encode the rule that a warning must be evaluated against the fold rather than the record. The missingFieldsWarning suite exists because that function was NOT fixed when its neighbour was; its sharpest case is 'reports only the fields still missing, not every field the spec omitted', which is what a passing-but-wrong implementation would fail.

summary: Pins every consumer to hooks/note-shape.mjs so a required field cannot go missing from one surface again: each spec example must contain the fields its own checksForSpec demands, the write guide and capture prompt must both carry every example verbatim, the MCP kb_write description must contain requiredFieldsLine(), and a dedicated suite asserts no surface says a flow's anchors come from its steps. It also carries the write-time warning contracts (flowStepsWarning/missingFieldsWarning judge the fold, not the spec). A newer describe block, 'kb repair-aliases surfaces agree with each other and with the frozen field name', extends the same drift-guard idea to a field note-shape.mjs's SPEC_SHAPES never covers directly: identityAliases only appears in the repair-aliases worklist/MCP tool/USER_COMMANDS text, not in any spec an agent writes, so it pins those three surfaces to each other by hand (the exact 'identityAliases' string, the empty-notebook sentinel 'No file/flow notes to reconcile.', the offset/limit MCP schema props, and the 'no aliases at all' line distinguishing it from kb repair's own missing-identity-aliases check) rather than deriving them from a table the way SPEC_SHAPES lets the rest of this file do.
